contract_plain_english: For a sound wave traveling to the right in one spatial dimension at positive sound speed c, an appropriate scalar combination w of pressure and particle velocity is modeled by w_t + c w_x = 0. The equation is scalar, first-order, constant-coefficient, and hyperbolic; it is called one-way because it isolates propagation in one direction. The plus sign together with c > 0 gives rightward motion, with translated profiles depending on x - c t. The cited passage leaves the generic formula for w and the exact regularity, initial, and boundary assumptions unstated, and it does not present an exhaustive physical or solution classification.

definitions_and_conventions: Subscripts t and x denote partial derivatives with respect to t and x.

details: There is one scalar time derivative and one scalar spatial derivative.
The spatial derivative is multiplied by the positive constant c and enters with a plus sign.
With c > 0, w_t + c w_x = 0 is the right-going one-way model at speed c.
The surrounding contrast w^2_t - c w^2_x = 0 is assigned speed -c and leftward propagation, confirming that the sign-coefficient pairing carries the direction semantics.
By the explicitly stated identity with the advection form, profiles depending on x - c t are admitted and propagate rightward without changing shape.
The source says such profiles are admitted; it does not explicitly formulate an if-and-only-if classification of all solutions.
The wave variable combines pressure and particle velocity rather than being identified with either quantity alone.
A full one-dimensional acoustic system contains both right-going and left-going characteristic combinations; equation (1.4) isolates one direction.
Equation (1.4) is scalar, first-order, homogeneous, constant-coefficient, and hyperbolic in the source's setting.
It is distinct from the later second-order wave equation used for bidirectional pressure waves.

undebatable_constraints: The displayed PDE must be w_t(x,t) + c w_x(x,t) = 0 with a plus sign before c w_x.
The right-going interpretation must retain c > 0 and propagation speed c.
The equation must remain scalar and first-order, not be replaced by the full two-equation acoustic system or by the second-order wave equation.
The variable w must retain its acoustic interpretation as an appropriate combination of pressure and particle velocity rather than pressure alone or particle velocity alone.
The term 'one-way' must retain the particular-direction interpretation; the source does not claim that the scalar equation by itself models simultaneous waves in both directions.
Any translated-profile statement must use x - c t for the positive-c right-going case and must not be strengthened beyond the source's admitted-solution wording without additional argument.
